# ARM lane architecture decision, advisory only (#603)

Source checks: v0.5 candidate 1de925f0308df16a4d67e3272a2a01de5ecb8e10, v0.4 #623 8e15e78f; both host_lanes.py blob bbe3c9b8a145100456f02753209e9c2a2423d3ef. v0.4 already runs macOS ARM64 with five independent clean lanes; v0.5 at reviewed head retains both ARM hosts as monoliths. Linux ARM64 remains monolithic in both. Do not introduce competing workflow changes during forward recovery.

## Observed evidence
Successful #625 run 45551176975 attempt 1, 89/89 jobs fetched, head 15d49fe2: macOS ARM64 producer 13.25m, moves 78.55m, print 41.0667m, validate 54.9333m, lower 123.6167m, join 0.55m. Allocated job-minutes 311.9667; execution envelope 05:10:11Z–07:14:24Z = 124.2167m. Linux ARM64 remained the last long host at 201.9833m. v0.5 monolith observations 182.62m and 166.8m; different heads and release lines, no causal comparison or gate-wide savings claim.

## Decision
1. Prefer evaluating the existing independent clean-build lane strategy over prematurely generalizing Intel binary transport. Native construction+execution and same-run receipt remain mandatory. Replicated setup/fixture work, actual queue and native concurrency are costs; no claim the split saves compute.
2. Before extending this runner, harden the existing join. Local Linux isolated reproduction of check_join (manually transcribed exact logic) accepted attempt 0, swapped assignments, producer absorbing conformance work, and a matching duplicated inventory/output. Valid passes; missing test and failed lane refuse. Prior attempt accepted without provider lineage (not inherently wrong to retain, but insufficient evidence of selected execution). Advisory script in dod8 extracts original function and fixtures; not a full module/host execution. Source also shows executed() erases ok/ignored/FAILED distinctions, no independent ignored list or per-target identity in the flattened workspace list. Distinct targets can legitimately have the same test name: bind target plus test, not a global unique-name rule. No observed production false pass; synthetic malformed receipt histories and coverage/attempt consistency limitations only.
3. Reuse the #628 attempt-aware principles once qualified, adapting to independent lanes with no construction artifact dependency: host/role/attempt-scoped artifact IDs and names, provider identity, complete selected execution records, exact head, target and run, strict positive attempt, all statuses and inventory per target, expected lane filters, producer cannot substitute conformance, explicit ignored inventory, archive hashes, exact command/exit evidence. Join must reject missing/duplicate receipts, foreign host, old failed retained execution, and unqualified nonexecution. No need for binary portability machinery in first candidate.
4. If clean lane pilot is too expensive, consider same-host construction transport. Intel implementation is macOS-specific: platform.system/machine, DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH/DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, otool -L/-l, dylib closure, receipt checks; Linux ELF loader/DT_NEEDED, interpreter, glibc/ABI and dependency closure need distinct validation; macOS ARM64 still needs architecture, toolchain, path and runner parity. Never copy Intel binaries across architectures. Require native evidence, exact source/toolchain and explicit closed dependency archive; do not use cross-run build outputs.
5. Qualification: preserve unsplit control and SPEC/terminal check names, same source and pin, compare complete per-target executed/ignored manifests, failures and doctests, deliberate planted failures, positive/negative retry and stale artifact tests, logs/resources/cost/queue, native coverage. No dispatch without separate authorization. Run independent host pilot only after release sequencing and #628/receipt review; do not merge from this advisory note.

## Limitations
Existing #625 split and v0.5 monolith observations are cross-revision. No new actual host tests or transport validation. Archive for #628 not delivered. Review of v0.4/v0.5 source is read-only.
